ranked_facts.concept_key: unilateral purulent discharge mixed with blood
ranked_facts.why: The presence of unilateral purulent discharge mixed with blood is more likely to be associated with a nasal foreign body, which would cause a localized infection, than with other candidates such as infectious processes of the nasal cavity, inflammatory processes, or neoplastic processes, which might present with more generalized symptoms.

Unilaterality of symptoms, such as discharge and pain, is more characteristic of an anatomical obstruction like a foreign body in the nasal cavity, which would affect one side more than the other, rather than conditions that typically cause bilateral symptoms.
